_about: Max damage plan per class (hand-written). Level order with the specialty picks at each skill level, what each step is worth, and what automating costs. The tables and chips beside this text read data/topplayers.json (NotMeter generation 82ac2ad73047b23f, Global top-20 parses per boss recorded Oct 11-15, published Oct 15; Korea top-20 builds). The written text quotes the audit's Oct 7-14 week (NotMeter generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4, parses Oct 11-13) unless it says otherwise, so a share or level in the text can differ by a few points from the table. 'gain' is an estimate of total DPS from that step for a player at the same gear, worked out as (that skill's share of damage) x (the measured change in its casts or damage per cast).

meta.week: Written text: Global week of Oct 7–14, 2026 (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4). Tables: generation 82ac2ad73047b23f (parses Oct 11–15)

chanter.sum: Every Chanter decision runs through Dark Crush. Option 5 (no cooldown, skill level 16) is worth more than anything else you can buy: median top-20 Global Chanters log 25 Dark Crush uses a minute in boss fights (the top 10% by damage at equal CP, 35), and players without it about 5–9. Get Dark Crush to 16 first, then Onslaught to 16 for Storm Chain (7.2% of damage). NotMeter ranks Chanter 1st of 8 (118.79; 114.08 after the Oct 13 patch) and +22.0% at equal CP. The percentages in this plan's text are from NotMeter's Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4); the table and chips follow the newest week.

order.why: 18.0% of damage, plus 13.5% from its Piercing Strike chain (31.5% together). Option 5 removes the cooldown, so every macro press inside a 2 s window is another Dark Crush (about 25 a minute against 5–9 without it). Option 3 made each Dark Crush hit 47% harder in the data. 96% of top Global Chanters are at 16+, 41% at 20.
steps: swap 4 for 5 (no cooldown). At equal combat power 3+5 vs 4+5 is +1–2%, within noise; Korea's Inven guide recommends 3+5 at 16

order.why: Your held left click. Option 4 cuts Spinning Strike's cooldown on every hit, which means more Dark Crush windows. Option 5 adds Storm Chain (7.2% of damage on its own); 70% of top Global Chanters are at 16+, and 4+5 is the most common pick (63%). The sheet says 20.
steps: −1 s Spinning Strike cooldown per hit

order.why: 11.9% of damage and your main Dark Crush opener (30 s cooldown, 25 s with option 1). Never drop option 1: players without it measured 4–5% lower. Option 5 made each cast 29% stronger; 48% of top Global Chanters are at 16+. Global 1+3 50%, 1+5 29%; Korea and the daevaos build run 1+3+5. A battle healer swaps 3 for 2 (+10% Heal Boost): derived, untested on Global.

The filler row. It is 12.4% of damage and its Bursting Blow chain 14.5% (26.9% together), so the Lv 16 multi-hit (+19% per cast) is worth it after the three above. 67% of top Global Chanters are at 16+, and 3+5 is 61%.
steps: −20% MP (option 4 is only an accuracy debuff)

order.why: 2% damage; it's here to open Dark Crush. 15 s cooldown (the Aug 26 cut to 10 s is not live). 67% of top Global Chanters run 3+4.

auto: Dark Crush, Piercing Strike, Spinning Strike, Impactful Crush and Incandescent Blow (with Bursting Blow) fire from the macro; Onslaught's chain, Storm Chain and Wind's Promise procs come from holding left click. Only Marchutan's Wrath and Rushing Smash (≈2% together) are left to press.

The stack order (Dark Crush first, then its two openers, then filler) is the same priority a perfect player follows, so the macro only gives up its 10 ms delay and the odd filler cast just before a window opens. Chanter is the most macro-friendly class in the game right now.

Whole boss fights, downtime included: median top-20 Global Chanter 25/min, top 10% by damage at equal CP 35/min. The few who hold 50–55/min in boss fights did ~20% more than their combat power predicts. Without option 5 you'll see about 5–9/min: that's normal until 16.

It opens a 3 s window but costs a cast and deals <1% at stigma level 1–5. Nearly every top Global Chanter slots it (97%); casters and non-casters differ by about −2% at equal power (not significant). This guide's rule, not the sheet's: press it between windows, when Spinning Strike and Impactful Crush are both on cooldown.
Global Chanters who used it measured 6–9% lower at equal combat power (NotMeter can't tell when it was used). Hold it only while a boss's stagger bar is up; the sheet lists it as N/A.
Undefeated Mantra and Sprint Mantra switch off on a second press, so they stay on their own keys with Power of the Storm.
Chanter as the main healer (no Cleric)

In the 565 Cleric-less Global parses that had a Chanter, the Chanter gave the most healing in 524 of the 526 with any healing between players (93% of all 565). Add Recuperation on cooldown (option 1 gives a second consecutive cast and stacks the heal over time twice) and, if you swap one in, Healing Touch for burst. The buffer four stays; damage share drops from 19.0% to 16.4%. Keep Recuperation and Healing Touch off the macro so you can time them. Spinning Strike option 2 for healing and Sprint Mantra 15 are derived from the DB and untested on Global.

Onslaught, Incandescent Blow with its chains and Heat Wave Blow hit up to 4 within 4 m; Spinning Strike, Marchutan's Wrath and Rushing Smash up to 4; Impactful Crush option 1 makes it an AoE. The same macro works on packs; no Global pack-clear test exists.
chanter.stig: Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4). Top 20 per boss, per player (104 players): Marchutan's Wrath about 97% (median 5), Undefeated Mantra about 96% (20; 98% counting a second Chanter's), Power of the Storm about 81% (20), Sprint Mantra 81% (10), Guardian Blessing 25% (15), Focused Defense 10% (5). Guardian Blessing is the swap: at equal CP its users (11 players) were about 9% ahead of Sprint Mantra users (71), averaged per player, 95% range −1% to +21%, not significant. Undefeated and Sprint are party buffs. The chips above read the newest week (parses Oct 11–15), so their shares and levels can differ from these Oct 7–14 numbers.

sorcerer.sum: Hellfire (21.7%), Blaze (14.7%), Fire Wall (13.1%), Bittercold Wind (9.2%), Firestorm (8.9%) and Cold Storm (6.5%) are 74% of a top Global Sorcerer's damage (post-patch: 22.4%, 15.0%, 11.4%, 9.4%, 9.1% and 6.3%). The rotation has two engines: every Firestorm cuts Hellfire's cooldown, and Flame Arrow's option 5 resets Blaze (option 4 adds +5% Fire damage for 10 s). Build those two first. The percentages in this plan's text are from NotMeter's Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4); the table and chips follow the newest week.

order.why: Option 4 takes 2 s off Hellfire per fireball. Each Firestorm throws 5 fireballs in Global parses, so one use can take up to 10 s off Hellfire; the top 10% get about 7.9 Hellfires a minute (all parses average 5.8). Global top: 2+4 55%, 4+5 37%; take 5 at 20 (+15% per fireball, up to +75%).

Your biggest hit (21.7% of damage). Option 5 (−15 s) gave 40% more Hellfires (5.6 vs 4.0 a minute); 72% of top Global Sorcerers are at 16+, and 1+5 is the most common pick (36%). Option 1 makes the charge faster, which matters because you hold it to Max every time.

Your held left click and its Pyroclasm chain. Option 4 is the Sep 16 version on Global: +5% Fire damage for 10 s per Pyroclasm (275 of 282 option-4 parses show the buff, none without), and Fire attacks now apply Fire Mark themselves; option 5 resets Blaze: 34% more Blaze casts. Global top: 4+5 for 70%. The top 10% cast 34 Blaze a minute vs 23 for the median player.

14.7% of damage. Option 4 (multi-hit) measured +26% per cast. At 16, Est (his guide is written for TW/KR) calls option 5 non-negotiable (−3 s Wish of Concentration per hit); 3+4 and 3+5 measured the same, so take 5 if you press Wish on cooldown. Global top: 3+5 53% (post-patch 42%); 77% are at 16+.
steps: −3 s Wish of Concentration per hit

order.why: +10% Attack (option 2) and +10% Combat Speed (option 4) on a buff Blaze keeps resetting. Korea runs it at 20 for −10 s on every cooldown. The buff lasts 10 s at level 1 (18 s at the Global median level 17). Global per player: 2+5 40%, 4+5 34%, 2+4 18%, 2+4+5 8%.
9.2% of damage, but its picks are cheap: 61% of top Global players run 1+4. Logged levels: median 15, about half at 16+; option 5 (16) is picked by only 2–3% (Korea's top 20: 60%).

auto: A macro fires it uncharged. By the database a Max cast does about 3× an uncharged one (1,137 vs 3,412 at level 1); Global Max casts have a median of 82.8k (middle half 71–100k), and uncharged casts are too rare in the logs to measure. Hellfire is 21.7% of damage. Keep it on its own key and hold it to Max.
Fire Wall + Cold Storm by hand

Together 19.6% of damage (13.1% + 6.5%; post-patch 11.4% + 6.3%), split between the ground hit and the Embers / Frostbite debuff. The top 10% land 35–37 hits a minute from each vs 24–29 for the median player. If you forget them when the boss moves, the 6-entry in-game macro (Other versions) fires them for you and loses less than missing casts.

Est's guide weaves Ice Chain on Global because cooldowns are long. Two thirds of top-10% parses don't cast it at all. When it is cast (36% of top parses), Ice Chain is about 5% of damage and its chained Cold Wave about 6% more, but those casts replace Flame Arrow and Blaze, and a +3% (±2.4) gain measured earlier is inside the noise. Skip it unless you're short on MP.
One filler line on the macro (Blaze, Firestorm, Winter's Shackles, Frost Burst) plus Flame Arrow held; everything that decides burst stays on keys you press so it lines up.

Global's maximum is about 19–21% (Korea 34–40%). Est's minimum for full Wish of Concentration uptime and the Bittercold Wind breakpoint is 25.6%, which Global can't reach yet, so take every source: the Illusion Mirror card, Talisra wings and cooldown-reduction Daevanion tiles.

Hellfire, Bittercold Wind, Ice Chain, Frost, Frost Burst and Winter's Shackles hit up to 4 within 4 m; Fire Wall up to 4 in a 1×10 m wall; Cold Storm up to 4 within 5 m plus Frostbite; Delayed Explosion becomes AoE at 15. Korean leveling guides use ice AoE until Flame Arrow reaches 16, and Est calls Ice Chain a mobbing skill. No Global pack-clear test exists, so the pack rotation is UNVERIFIED.
sorcerer.stig: Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4). Top 20 per boss: Element Enhancement 97% (median 20), Fire Wall 100% (median 11), Delayed Explosion 97% (median 10), Cold Storm 90% (median 5); post-patch Fire Wall 100%, Element Enhancement 98%, Delayed Explosion 97%, Cold Storm 87%. Players without Cold Storm measured ~3% lower. Hibernation (27%) and Steel Barrier (11%) show up as swaps. Same 4 as this page.

ranger.sum: Deadshot (23.5%) and Tempest Shot (16.6%) carry the class, then Drill Dart (10.9%) and Hunter's Soul procs (6.5%). The cheapest big upgrade in the game is Snipe option 4 at skill level 12: it cuts Deadshot's cooldown on every Snipe hit, and Global Rangers with it cast 2.3x as many Deadshots. The percentages in this plan's text are from NotMeter's Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4); the table and chips follow the newest week.

order.why: Your held left click. Option 4 (−1 s Deadshot cooldown per hit) is why top Rangers fire a median 8.4 Deadshots a minute (top 10% of Global parses at equal CP). Option 5 at 16 adds the Tempest Arrow chain (3.3% of damage; the top 10% cast it 13 times a minute). Global top: 4+5 for 64%; 69% picked option 5, so at least 16.

Option 5 adds a second hit: +53% damage per Deadshot in the data. Option 2 speeds up the charge; option 3 lets you charge while moving (Global top players: 2+5 38%, 2+3 24%, 2+3+5 15%; Allyria's order is 2, 2+3, 2+3 at 16, 2+3+5).
Option 5 fires Drill Dart twice: ~1.9x damage per cast. Players with 3+5 measured ~5% ahead of 3+4 at equal power. Global top: 3+5 44%; 67% picked option 5.

Your most-cast skill (~100 a minute). Option 3 measured +9% per cast; option 5 gave 12% more casts. 85% of top Global Rangers picked option 5 (so at least 16); 3+5 is the most common pick (55%). Option 2 (+10% crit) is the last pick; the crit-cap reason is this page's inference.

Gale is +7% Combat Speed and +7% PvE damage. Option 5 (−10 s) gave 1.9x the casts, which keeps it up the whole fight. 69% of top Global players picked option 5; 4+5 is the most common (62%). Option 1 (+5 s) is only for early on.
4.1% of damage; 3+4 is what 52% of top Global Rangers run (Allyria's 4+5 at 16 is only 10%). Option 5 at 16 (25% chance to reset) gave 26% more casts if you have levels to spare; 21% picked it.

auto: A macro fires it uncharged: about a third of a Max cast by the tooltip (599 vs 1,798). Global macro-only parses land at roughly 40–90% of a Max cast per cast, a small sample of 4 players. Deadshot is 23.5% of damage, so the range is this page's arithmetic: 23.5% times a 10–67% shortfall. Hold it yourself.

The Global sheet and the Korean Aug 30 post both put Tempest Shot under Drill Dart in the same line. An older Korean 'Tempest Shot cancel' rule (Tempest Shot in its own entry, about +3%) is contradicted by both, so this page's Late card no longer uses it.

Allyria says buffs in the macro are fine because you run boss to boss, and the Korean Aug 30 author keeps them in too. Vaizel's Authority, Bow of Blessing and Supporting Fire fire on cooldown, which top players do anyway (Supporting Fire 47 hits/min for the top 10%). Check your hit counts on the dummy; if they drop, press the buffs yourself.

Tempest Shot, Drill Dart, Gale Arrow, Snare Shot, Burst Arrow and Griffon Arrow hit up to 4 within 4 m of the target; Explosion Trap up to 4 within 5 m (option 1 pulls); Arrow Storm up to 4. Allyria's order: Explosion Trap to group, then Snare Shot (Slow) → Burst Arrow and Griffon Arrow, then the held Snipe + macro. For farming she suggests holding only the in-game macro key without Deadshot. No Global pack-clear test exists, so the order is UNVERIFIED.

Save Arrow Storm (50 stagger), Explosive Arrow (20), Griffon Arrow (20), Burst Arrow (15) and Deadshot (10–16) for stagger bars. Arrow Scattershot is only for broken (staggered) bosses, as cooldown, HP and MP refill (Allyria).
ranger.stig: Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4). Top 20 per boss: Vaizel's Authority 97% (median 20), Supporting Fire 96% (buff median 10, mode 15), Bow of Blessing 96% (15), Griffon Arrow 72% (15), Explosive Arrow 30%. At equal CP the two 4th picks are even: Griffon users (72 players) vs Explosive users (29), +0.1% per player, 95% range −6% to +6%. Arrow Storm and Mother Nature's Breath: 0 of 106 top Global Rangers. Same 4 as this page.

assassin.sum: Heart Gore (28%) and Insignia Explosion (20%) are about half your damage, and you have to hit from behind: top Global Assassins land 85% of hits on the back. Heart Gore fires off crits, so it runs itself once your crit is high. The real upgrades are Insignia Explosion casts (Quick Slice option 4, then Insignia Explosion option 5) and pressing Illusive Clone: the top 10% log 2.9 casts a minute against 1.2 for the median. The percentages in this plan's text are from NotMeter's Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4); the table and chips follow the newest week.

order.why: Your held left click. Option 4 takes 1 s off Insignia Explosion per hit: players with it cast 1.55x as many Insignia Explosions. Option 5 (guaranteed crit) didn't raise Heart Gore casts in the data, so it can wait.
steps: −1 s Insignia Explosion cooldown per hit

order.why: 20% of damage. Option 5 (−3 s) gave 35% more casts; option 2 (multi-hit) +12% per cast. 2+5 and 2+3 measured even, 3+5 ~5% lower, so always keep 2.

Your biggest skill. Option 4 (multi-hit) measured +21% per cast. Option 5 (reset on crit) only added ~6% more casts on Global, because your crit already brings it back fast; take it at 16, not before Insignia Explosion.

The Savage Roar chain is ~10% of damage. 2+4 measured 3–4% ahead of 2+3: option 4 gave 1.5x Shadowstrikes, and Shadowstrike's option 2 is +20% crit damage for 10 s (live on Global; the aion2.app database still says 5 s).
2% of damage, only on staggered bosses; 4+5 is the most common pick on Global (45%) and what Korea runs. 69% of top Global players use it and 56% of those are at 16.

auto: Top Global Assassins: 85% of hits from behind, 8% from the front. Rear Smite, Ambush (+30%) and Triniel's Dagger (+30%) are back-attack skills, and Korea's top 20 put Back Attack Damage Boost on every manastone. Every hit from the front loses all of that.

Removes Heart Gore's cooldown and adds 20% of your damage for 10 s at stigma level 1 (20 s at 20). NotMeter logs 2.9 casts a minute for the top 10% and 1.2 for the median: real casts of 1–3 per fight, and the rate looks high because 73% of these fights last under 90 s. Press it with Swift Contract.
Macro line with Ambush in row 1

At equal CP, Global Ambush users trail on all 15 bosses (per player about -7%: 86 players with Ambush vs 51 without; 95% range about -14% to 0%), and only 4 of the top-10% parses use it. Its option 1 engraves 2 Insignias on a back attack, but the data doesn't show a gain. It's the Korean Sep 30 optimizer line, kept under Other versions. This is observational data.
Heart Gore is crit-triggered and everything else in the line is priority-ordered, so the macro plays it the way you would. What the macro can't do is stand behind the boss or time Illusive Clone.

The held Quick Slice + macro line hits 4 targets: the Quick Slice chain, Savage Roar chain, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion and Savage Fang all hit up to 4 within 4 m. Flash Slice hits up to 4 (option 4 adds a second use), Whirlwind Slice option 2 is an AoE, and Throw Shadowblade (stigma) resets on kill at 10 and goes AoE at 20; Korean guides call it essential for field farming. No Global pack-clear test exists.
assassin.stig: Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4). Top 20 per boss, per player: Illusive Clone 98% (median 20), Swift Contract 95% (median 15), Triniel's Dagger 91%, then Evasion Stance 47% (median 5) or Savage Fang 43% (median 15) as the 4th. Evasion Stance is the survival pick; Savage Fang is the damage pick (it engraves 5 Insignias). At equal CP the two can't be separated: Fang users were 4–5% behind per player and 6–7% ahead per parse. Fang appears in 15 of the 30 top-10% parses, Evasion Stance in 2.

gladiator.sum: Overhead Slam and its Upward Strike chain are 61% of a Gladiator's damage (33.5% + 27.4%). Option 3 (the Upward Strike chain) at skill level 8 and option 5 (no cooldown) at 16 aren't optional. Every top Global Gladiator has Overhead Slam at 16+, and 54% have it at 20. The percentages in this plan's text are from NotMeter's Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4); the table and chips follow the newest week.

order.why: Option 3 adds Upward Strike, 27% of damage by itself. Option 4 (crit) measured +31% per cast. Option 5 removes the cooldown so it can be spammed in every Rage Burst window. The top 10% log about 67 Overhead Slam uses a minute. Global picks: 3+4+5 54%, 3+5 27%, 4+5 18%.

The other half of the Overhead Slam ↔ Rending Blow alternation (~57 uses a minute for the top 10%), plus its Smashing Blow chain: 20% of damage together (9.5% + 10.8%). 83% of top Global players have option 5. Option 5 restores MP on crits; the Global sheet warns you'll run short on MP until you have it.

7.8% of damage plus Prepare for Battle (+20% PvE damage for 20 s on a 45 s cooldown). The buff logs the real skill level: top Global median 16 (69% at 16+, 33% picked option 5), so 12 is not the stop point. Option 4 measured +21% per cast.
Only usable on staggered targets. Korea runs 4+5 at 16; on Global it's 1.2% of damage, and 20% of top players are at 16+.

auto: The macro alternates the two (the 内絕 cancel). The top 10% log about 67 Overhead Slam and 57 Rending Blow uses a minute in boss fights (uses logged, not hits). If you're well under 45 Overhead Slams, the macro isn't reaching its Overhead Slam entry often enough.

The Global sheet's layout leaves it to you. Prepare for Battle is +20% PvE damage, and top players keep it up (NotMeter logs 3.0 uses a minute, more than a 45 s cooldown allows, so read it as uses logged, not casts), so this page fires it from the macro's first entry.
Top Global Gladiators cast Keen Strike ~3 times a minute: the macro keeps them busy. Hold it only while you're short on MP (before Rending Blow option 5).

Gladiators hold the boss in 55% of Templar-less parties (908 of 1,644) with the same stigmas and rotation. Three changes: pull with Leaping Slam (option 1 gives 3 s of Prepare for Battle) then Ruinous Blow; keep Rage Burst on cooldown, since Wounded cuts the boss's Attack and it enables Overhead Slam; press Focused Block yourself before heavy hits. Derived from the skill effects, untested.

Rending Blow with its Smashing Blow chain hits up to 4 targets within 4 m, Crushing Wave up to 4 within 5 m (option 4 resets it on crit), Lifestealing Blade up to 4 within 4 m, and Murderous Burst fires every 5 hits on up to 4 within 5 m. Overhead Slam option 2 makes it an AoE but costs the Upward Strike, crit and no-cooldown picks; Leaping Slam option 5 pulls enemies together. No Global pack-clear test exists. From the skill text: gather with Leaping Slam, open with Ruinous Blow (it also hits up to 4), keep the Rending Blow filler going, then add Crushing Wave and Lifestealing Blade.
gladiator.stig: Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4). Top Global Gladiators (top 20 per boss, per player): Lunge Stance 97% (median level 20), Rage Burst 99% (most at 5), Zikel's Blessing 94% (median 15), then Focused Block 64% (median 5) as the 4th. Wave Armor is rare (15%); at equal CP its users were 3–4% ahead of Focused Block users per player (re-check +2.6%, range −8% to +15%), which the data can't tell from zero. Lifestealing Blade (27%) was 1.5% behind Focused Block per player and the sign flips under another grouping, so there is no difference.

templar.sum: Judgment is 42.5% of a Templar's damage, and option 5 (no cooldown, skill level 16) gives five times the Judgments. Before 16 it's a different class. Second is Vicious Strike option 4 at skill level 12: Warding Strike's cooldown drops on every hit, and each Warding Strike opens Judgment. The percentages in this plan's text are from NotMeter's Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4); the table and chips follow the newest week.

order.why: 38 Judgments a minute with option 5 vs 8 without. Options 3 and 4 measured about the same (+5–7% per cast); Global top picks: 3+4+5 36%, 3+5 34%, 4+5 27%.
Your held left click. Option 4 (−2 s Warding Strike per hit) gave 2.5x Warding Strikes and 1.6x Judgments. Option 5 adds Threatening Blow (4.4% of damage). Global top picks: 4+5 50%, 3+4 32%.
steps: −2 s Warding Strike cooldown per hit

order.why: Pummel and its Punishing Strike are 11% of damage (4.6% + 6.0%). Option 4 (−1 s Punishment cooldown on hit) is the Sep 16 text and Global logs agree: holders cast Punishment 2.3 times a minute vs 1.7–1.8.
11.5% of damage. Any cast gives Executor, but a Max cast does about three times an uncharged one, so charge it on its own key. Option 5 measured +29% per cast; option 3 charges faster.
Opens Judgment. Option 1 gave 24% more casts. Its cooldown stays 30 s on Global (Korea's 25 s cut isn't live), so option 1's −5 s matters.
Also opens Judgment and stuns for Annihilate. Option 4 gave 22% more casts. Global top picks: 3+4 56%, 2+4 36% (option 2 removes the MP cost: use it if you run short).

auto: Uncharged Punishment does about a third of a Max (database 1,268 vs 3,805; 26–44% in Global parses, depending on the method), and it's 11.5% of damage. Keep it on its own key.
Under 1% of damage, and its −25% Defense barely matters on bosses (Defense only removes 10% of its value in PvE), so dropping it costs little. The sheet keeps it on row 2 of the Banner entry.
Annihilate on row 0 fires on cooldown, and Judgment on row 1 of the same entry casts the moment a shield attack opens a window, which is what you'd do by hand.

Vicious Strike with its chains, and Pummel with Punishing Strike, hit up to 4 targets within 4 m; Warding Strike hits up to 4 within 5 m; Punishment up to 4 within 4 m of its target; Grapple (stigma) pulls up to 4 within 7 m. Shield Smite option 5 is an AoE stun and Annihilate option 5 an AoE. No Global pack-clear test exists. From the skill text: Poach or Doom Shield to pull, Warding Strike, then the held Vicious Strike + macro line with a charged Punishment on the group.
templar.stig: Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4). Top 20 per boss, per player: Noble Armor 89% (median 15), Doom Shield 77% (about 14), Taunt 77% (12% at 20, 44% at 15–19), Battlefield Banner 77% (18–20), Shield of Protection 46% (about 8). Across all parties Taunt is 76–78%. At equal CP, Banner users were 2–3% ahead of Shield of Protection users per player, which isn't significant.

spiritmaster.sum: Spiritmaster damage is spread out: Elemental Fusion 17.0%, Combustion 7.6% (+6.8% from its Ashy Call chain), Dimensional Control 7.5%, the Ancient Spirit's attacks about 15% and the Fire Spirit about 11%. About a third of it lands whatever you press (spirit basic attacks ~13% plus the spirit skills they fire by themselves ~21%), so the macro matters less than on any other class. Get Combustion to 16 for Ashy Call first. The percentages in this plan's text are from NotMeter's Oct 7–14 week (generation 7a95660ba62a7ef4); the table and chips follow the newest week.

order.why: Your filler (7.6% of damage). Option 5 adds Ashy Call (6.8% of damage, 30 casts a minute); option 4 gave 23% more casts. Global top: 4+5 52%; 70% are at 16+.

Your biggest hit (17.0% of damage), fed by every spirit skill. Option 3 measured +12% per cast. Leave option 4 (charge) alone: a macro can't charge it (Sirin leaves it out too). Global, among the 175 parses with readable picks: 3+5 46%, 2+3 24%, 2+5 14%, 2+3+5 12%; Sirin's order is 2, 2+3, 2+5, 2+3+5. 50% of players are at 16+.
Korea's top 20 run it at 20 (2+3+5). The Fire Spirit's skills and basic attacks are ~10.9% of damage. Global top: 2+3 62%, 2+5 26%; 34% are at 16+.
3.0% of damage plus the Curse; 49% of top Global players run 3+4.
Held left click. 74% of top Global players run 3+4 (+2% Attack stacks from Earth Tremor, up to 5).

Sirin's 16 priority with Combustion and Elemental Fusion: -1 s on all cooldowns per hit, 'crucial early'. It is the way to shorten the Ancient Spirit's downtime on Global (cooldown reduction is only about 19–21%). Fire it during boss stagger.

auto: Spirit basic attacks and the skills spirits fire by themselves (15% chance per hit; Ancient Spirit every 7 attacks) land whatever you press, so Spiritmaster loses the least when the macro (or you) slip.

Its Plasma Cannon, Destruction and basic attacks are about 15% of damage, and every skill it uses grants Four Elements. The top 10% get 25% more Plasma Cannons than the median. On Global it has a 90 s cooldown and lasts 30 s, so low cooldown reduction (about 19–21%) leaves it 'substantial downtime'. Cast Benediction first: spirit stats are snapshotted when they're summoned.
Option 4 turns it into a charge skill; a macro would fire it uncharged (this page's reading; Sirin leaves option 4 out).

Sirin gives two setups: Option 1 (in-game macro only) and Option 2 (mouse software that fires Destructive Attack at max charge, skill queue OFF). She says they 'perform similarly', Option 2 slightly ahead, and warns Option 2 misfires when the frame rate drops. External software is a ban risk on Global (NC's unauthorized-program rule; macros named in the Oct 10, Oct 12 and Oct 14 ban waves), so Option 1 is the safe default.

Light of Protection vs Noble Aura

Per player, Clerics with Noble Aura (70 players) deal about 12% more personal damage than those with Light of Protection (8), but 177 of the 186 Noble Aura parses had an Undefeated Mantra Chanter and 14 of the 19 Light of Protection parses had none. Controlling for that the gap is +3% (95% range −5% to +11%), not significant, and the meter can't see Light of Protection's party-wide buff (17.5% at level 15). Keep it when no Chanter covers it.
Light of Regeneration in the macro

The sheet runs it in macro entry 2 (30 s cooldown) when starting out and casts it by hand later. Top Clerics cast it 1.85 times a minute (cap 2), Debilitating Mark 5.5 (cap 6) and Earth Punishment 2.2 (cap 2). Divine Aura is in 99% of long top parses, so it does fire from the macro.

81% of single-Cleric Global parties have a Mantra Chanter; there Clerics run Light of Protection only 20% of the time, against 94% with no Chanter. With both, only the higher level applies and Undefeated Mantra wins a tie. Earth's Blessing and a Chanter's Power of the Storm can't both be on a party member: Earth's Blessing covers 27% of a fight with a Storm Chanter and 37% without. A Chanter's Earth's Promise doesn't apply together with Chain of Torment.

Condemnation, Judgment Thunder, Bolt, Chain of Torment and Debilitating Mark hit up to 4 targets within 4 m; Divine Aura option 2 makes it an AoE. Korea's guide uses Judgment Thunder for trash. No Global pack-clear test exists.
